  "text": "On Sunday, Mara came home from the library at half past three. She had stayed to mend the spine of a book no one had borrowed in years. The glue was still tacky when she left it beneath a stack of dictionaries.

At home, she put the kettle on and carried the suitcase into the hall. Its broken wheel had left a dark mark on the floorboards. She rubbed at it with her thumb, then moved the suitcase beside the umbrella stand, where it was less in the way.

The telephone rang at ten minutes past four.

He apologized for being late, though she had not been counting. His neighbor had needed help bringing in her shopping. Mara pictured him climbing the stairs with bags in both hands and wondered whether his knee had troubled him. She did not ask.

They spoke about the library book she had found in the parcel. He remembered borrowing it, but not why he had kept it. Its due date was stamped twenty-three years earlier. Mara told him she had returned it that morning, without a fine. He said she had always been good at knowing which rules mattered.

She looked down at the mark on the floor. For a while, neither of them said anything.

Then he asked if she might like to meet for tea one day. Mara could hear a bus stopping outside his window. She said there was a café across from the library, and that Thursday was her early day.

After the call, she made tea. The kettle had already boiled, but the water was still hot."
